doc: RTAI-003 baseline for crates/anvil-intercept/benches/midedit_roundtrip.rs. Compared against by scripts/check-midedit-baseline.sh during the bench.yml workflow. ADR-031 primary SLO / CI hard-fail is validation.roundtrip p95 (interactive-buffer <= 80 ms); validation.service p95 (<= 50 ms) is attribution and soft-warns only. This file's per-case p95 is the drift-warn anchor.

calibration.runner_note: Baseline captured on a developer Ubuntu 24.04 / x86_64 box (2026-04-30). GitHub Actions ubuntu-24.04 / ubuntu-latest produce different numbers -- nightlies were false-failing when the gate hard-failed on validation.service near_cap (~55 ms vs 50) while validation.roundtrip stayed under 80 ms. CI now hard-fails only on roundtrip SLO (ADR-031 primary boundary); service SLO breaches are soft-warn attribution. A GHA rebaseline on the dedicated LINUX_RUNNER class is still owed once a full midedit_roundtrip capture is recorded and committed; until then, drift WARNs after runner-class changes remain advisory. Do not pretend this file is a GHA-captured baseline.

tolerance.policy: p95 drift outside +/-drift_pct is a soft warning (CI passes). CI hard-fail requires a validation.roundtrip p95 that exceeds the ADR-031 SLO recorded in .slos (primary boundary). validation.service p95 over its .slos entry is soft-warn attribution only -- do not fail the nightly solely on service near_cap when roundtrip is still under SLO. Product ADR-031 numbers are unchanged; this is CI-gate alignment with the primary boundary. p50 and p99 are recorded for context but not gated -- see ADR-031 Regression policy. When a baseline p95 is 0 ms (sub-resolution case) the comparator switches from percentage drift to an absolute floor: a soft warn fires if observed p95 exceeds zero_baseline_floor_ms.

binary_short_circuit.note: Binary short-circuit returns before the rule pipeline runs; sub-microsecond cost is below the wall-clock resolution. With a zero baseline the comparator switches to the absolute-floor mode (.tolerance.zero_baseline_floor_ms): a soft warn fires if observed p95 exceeds the floor. Service SLO (50 ms) is attribution soft-warn only; CI hard-fail is validation.roundtrip.
